FeSe1-xTex single crystals with 0.4 ≤ x ≤ 1.0 were successfully grown using an optical zone-melting technique.
Plate-like crystals of FeSe0.7Te0.3 with dimensions up to 1 × 3 mm^2 were obtained.
The superconducting transition temperatures (Tc,onset) ranged from 8.9 K for x = 0.3 to 13-14 K for 0.5 < x < 0.7, and 11.5 K for x = 0.9.
The superconducting transition widths (ΔTc) were very narrow, in the range of 2-3 K.
Post-annealing temperatures were found to be critical for obtaining uniform and homogeneous single crystals.
The FeSe0.3Te0.7 crystal showed a distorted structure with a space group of P112/n at room temperature, indicating local lattice strain due to Te substitution.
Crystallization was successful for higher Te concentrations (x > 0.3) due to the lower melt viscosity.
The zero-field-cooled magnetic susceptibility showed a more pronounced diamagnetic response when the field was applied parallel to the crystal c-axis, indicating anisotropic magnetism.
The critical current density at 2 K reached values on the order of 10^3 A/cm^2 for the x = 0.5 crystal.

The upper critical field (Hc2) values of the FeSe1-xTex crystals were exceptionally large, comparable to polycrystalline samples, and increased with increasing Te concentration after a threshold of x = 0.3.
Evaporation of constituent elements, including Se and Te, was not an issue in the local heating of the ampoule during the optical zone-melting process.
The use of reacted or unreacted powders as starting materials did not influence the crystallinity and uniformity of the crystals.
The FeSe0.3Te0.7 sample seemed to be the best controlled growth, with a relatively high Tc, sharp superconducting transition, good crystallinity, and high phase stability.
The small drop in resistivity near 35 K, as reported for FeTe crystals, was not observed in the x = 0.9 FeSe1-xTex crystal.
The first-order resistive transition occurring near 65 K in the FeTe crystal was similar to previous reports.
